sourceName: National Health and Aging Trends Study
protocolPurpose: Define the minimum survey-design gate required before any NHATS R13/R14 cohort-flow, functional-survival, missingness or model-calibration output can be interpreted as a design-aware weighted estimate rather than an unweighted internal diagnostic.

currentDecision.reason: The survey-design protocol is registered, but exact round-specific weight, strata, PSU/variance-unit, variance method, eligible sample, missingness route map, disclosure validation and weighted-estimator script are not complete. Only synthetic validator tests are allowed.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Round-specific analysis weight
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Exact NHATS R13/R14 weight variable selected from Colectica/codebook and matched to the intended target population and analysis file.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Stratum field
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Exact stratum or variance-stratum field confirmed for the selected public-use file and round.

requiredDesignComponents.label: PSU / variance unit / cluster field
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Exact PSU, variance unit or cluster field confirmed for the selected public-use file and round.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Variance estimation method
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Taylor linearization, replicate weights or another survey-package-compatible method selected and documented with NHATS method source.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Domain / subpopulation rule
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Eligible R13/R14 subpopulation rule defined without dropping design information in a way that invalidates variance estimation.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Missingness and interview-route rule
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Death, proxy interview, residential care, nonresponse and not-classifiable routes mapped before any weighted rate, curve or missingness table.

requiredDesignComponents.label: R13/R14 linkage rule
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Baseline R13 sample-person records and R14 follow-up/endpoint routes linked through confirmed join keys and file tiers.

requiredDesignComponents.label: Finite population and inference boundary
requiredDesignComponents.minimumEvidence: Target population, finite population interpretation and design-aware uncertainty boundary documented before population inference.

readinessGates.requiredEvidence: Technical Paper 55 / sample-design documentation reviewed for the selected round, file and variance method.
Exact design variables confirmed through NHATS Cross-Year Search / Colectica or official codebooks.
R13/R14 analysis weight selected for the target population and file family.
Strata and PSU/variance-unit fields confirmed and not inferred from prose alone.
Taylor linearization, replicate-weight or equivalent survey-design variance method selected.
Domain/subpopulation handling rule documented before weighted estimation.
Endpoint, death, proxy, facility, nonresponse and not-classifiable routes mapped.
Disclosure-control validator passed for intended aggregate output envelope.
Weighted estimator script reviewed against survey-design, disclosure and no-individual-prediction gates.

prohibitedActions: Do not report weighted NHATS counts before the survey-design protocol is ready.
Do not report weighted curves or design-based confidence intervals before weights, strata, PSU/variance unit and variance method are confirmed.
Do not make population-inference, calibration, validation or treatment-effect claims from unweighted internal diagnostics.
Do not use candidate field patterns as confirmed variable names.
Do not export row-level NHATS records or upload NHATS data to public AI systems.
Do not output individual death dates, personal medical advice or personal longevity rankings.
nextWork: Confirm exact R13/R14 design variables through Colectica/codebooks before any weighted estimate.
Select a variance method and document whether it uses Taylor linearization, replicate weights or another survey-package-compatible approach.
Bind the survey-design gate to missingness, endpoint routing and disclosure-control validation.
Keep the validator synthetic-only until a governed workspace and reviewed estimator script exist.
